transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-13
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Marta Reyes (Crestline Head of ML), Liam O'Donnell (Infra), Sara Kim (PM), Dev Patel (SRE)

Summary:
Quick kickoff to align on workload portrait (QPS, concurrency shape, token distribution), agree success criteria for POC benchmarking and define milestones for an in-cloud pilot. Customer emphasized tail latency and HIPAA-ish compliance constraints; interested in dedicated pool if cost/lats match.

Topics covered:
- Current production shape and unknowns (burstiness, diurnal, tail)
- Benchmarks: end-to-end p95/p99, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens
- Input/output token distribution and prompt variability
- Success criteria for pilot and rollout timeline
- Security: audit logs, KMS, VPC/connectivity

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan Ellis: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh let's do quick intros then jump into the workload portrait.
[00:08] Marta Reyes: Hi this is Marta, I run ML at Crestline. Thanks Jordan.
[00:12] Liam O'Donnell: Liam here, infra lead.
[00:15] Sara Kim: Sara, product.
[00:16] Dev Patel: Dev, SRE.
[00:18] Priya Nair: Priya from Redwood - I'll drive the technical bits today. Diego as well is on hand for deep infra questions.
[00:25] Jordan Ellis: Great. Quick agenda: we want to understand your QPS baseline and bursts, typical request/response lengths, what a successful pilot looks like, then agree next steps. Is that good?
[00:34] Marta Reyes: Yep, perfect.
[00:36] Liam O'Donnell: Works for us.

[02:00] Priya Nair: Marta can you paint the current traffic picture - avg QPS, peak, how concurrent requests map to business events?
[02:08] Marta Reyes: Sure uh rough numbers: baseline is like 5 rps, we get sustained daytime of 8-12 rps, but the tricky bit is the bursts - marketing campaigns or lab batch jobs create spikes to ~120 rps for short windows, say 90 to 300 seconds. There's also a long-tail of very large prompts where outputs get very long.
[02:33] Jordan Ellis: When you say very large prompts what's the typical token mix input vs output?
[02:38] Marta Reyes: Input average 120 tokens, output average 450 tokens but 10% of requests end up 1,200 to 2,000 tokens output when clinical notes are expanded. Also, about 5% of calls are embeddings only for search.
[03:00] Priya Nair: Okay that's useful. Any hard latency SLOs? p95, p99?
[03:06] Dev Patel: We want p95 < 250ms for short replies (say <200 output tokens) for interactive clinician workflows. For long generations we tolerate higher but p99 shouldn't exceed 4.5s ideally. Those are stretch but target.
[03:23] Diego Alvarez: Quick clarification - p95 at the token level or request end-to-end?
[03:28] Dev Patel: End-to-end from API call to final token.

[05:00] Sara Kim: On success criteria - pilot needs to show comparable quality to current baseline, cost per consult under X (we gave a target number in the NDA), and stable tail latency during bursts. Also compliance: logs, SSO and audit, if those pass we'll consider dedicated.
[05:28] Jordan Ellis: Understood. For the pilot we'll aim to quantify three axes: correctness/quality (via eval set of 100 golden prompts), latency behavior (p50/p95/p99 across day + burst), and unit economics (cost per 1,000 tokens and cost per consult).

[07:00] Priya Nair: Let's discuss workload modeling. We'll want a 7-day traffic sample (even aggregated per-minute QPS is fine) plus a sample of representative prompts with input/output lengths. From that we build a synthetic replay to exercise tails.
[07:18] Marta Reyes: We can extract a week from our prod proxy and scrub PHI; we'll anonymize and provide the distribution.
[07:25] Liam O'Donnell: Note we have on-prem connector for SSO and restricted egress in our VPC - so private deployment might be necessary if the hosted path can't meet audit constraints.
[07:38] Jordan Ellis: Good to know. We'll include both hosted and dedicated pilot variants in the plan.

[09:00] Priya Nair: For sizing, two quick heuristics: concurrency = QPS * avg latency (in seconds). With your baseline 10 rps and target avg latency of 0.25s that'd be ~2.5 concurrency; but bursts at 120 rps with longer latencies obviously push concurrency and require more workers. Caching and KV reuse for repeated prefixes can reduce effective token compute.
[09:30] Marta Reyes: We do have reuse - many prompts share templates, so a lot of prefix caching could help. But the clinical expansion requests differ a lot.
[09:40] Priya Nair: Noted. We'll estimate caching hit rate from the sample prompts. Also we need to know distribution of sequence lengths — do you have histograms?
[09:50] Marta Reyes: We'll export pcts - 50/90/99 for input and output tokens. Expect median outputs ~420, 90th ~1,100, 99th ~1,900.

[11:00] Diego Alvarez: Question about benchmarking: do you want us to run model variants? quantized vs unq?
[11:06] Marta Reyes: Yes cost matters so we'd like to compare smaller quantized variants if quality isn't degraded. Also we want to test fallback behaviors if a model is overloaded.
[11:14] Jordan Ellis: We'll include 3 model profiles: high-quality (larger), mid (quantized), and a latency-optimized variant with reduced context. We'll also run a fallback policy test.

[13:00] Priya Nair: On burst handling we recommend 2 strategies: short-term autoscale plus emergency degrade to a faster model or increased batching with tail-aware shaping. For your 120 rps 3 minute bursts we can simulate and show expected p95/p99 under different policies.
[13:25] Dev Patel: How much lead time for autoscale? We prefer warm pools; cold spin-up can spike p99s.
[13:32] Priya Nair: Right — warm dedicated pools or reserved capacity for critical windows is recommended. If hosted-only, we can do reserved burst capacity / pre-warm flows. We'll propose a warm pool config.

[15:00] Jordan Ellis: Pricing note: for dedicated pools we show amortized cost per 1M tokens including infra and support. For hosted we'll show per-token plus optional priority capacity add-on.
[15:12] Marta Reyes: Competitor question - we've looked at Anthropic and BigCloud AI for latency. How do you differ on predictability?
[15:20] Jordan Ellis: Redwood focuses on predictable inference economics and fallbacks. Our smart routing and caching are designed to keep tail behavior stable, and we expose telemetry per-route. We'll show traces in the pilot.

[17:00] Priya Nair: Security checklist: SSO + SAML, SOC2 attestation, customer-managed KMS, audit logs retained 90+ days. Is that in line with your needs?
[17:12] Liam O'Donnell: Yes but we may need 1-year retention on audit logs for some flows. Also requirement for VPC peering for private deployment.
[17:20] Jordan Ellis: We'll escalate retention ask with security; we do have options for extended retention as an add-on.

[19:00] Marta Reyes: Timeline — we want a pilot report within 3 weeks of sample handoff. Is that feasible?
[19:08] Priya Nair: Typical cadence: sample + prompts -> 3 business days to synthesize replay and config -> 1 week of runs -> 2-3 days to analyze. So roughly 12 business days. If we start 2027-01-18 (sample delivered) we can have a report by end of month.
[19:30] Jordan Ellis: We'll aim for that. Also need to surface quality regressions vs your golden set; we'll run automated eval diffs.

[21:00] Dev Patel: For pilot we need network diagrams and egress policy to be correct — I'll send the template.
[21:08] Liam O'Donnell: I'll fill it out.

[23:00] Priya Nair: A few measurement details to confirm: we'll capture p50/p95/p99 request latencies, token throughput (tokens/sec per worker), GPU utilization, and cost per 1k tokens. Also we'll include tail latency heatmaps and concurrency quantiles.
[23:25] Marta Reyes: Sounds good. Can you also surface how batching choices impact quality/latency tradeoff?
[23:30] Priya Nair: Yep we'll include a table that shows expected latency and cost by batching window and max batch size. Expect non-linear improvements but also increased p99 if batching delay is too large.

[25:00] Jordan Ellis: Any blockers on data sharing or compliance?
[25:04] Marta Reyes: We'll need to scrub PHI; security is ok with that. Legal will want the security pack and SOC2 doc.
[25:12] Jordan Ellis: We'll send security pack and SOC2 link after the call.

[28:00] Diego Alvarez: One more note: KV cache effectiveness depends on prompt prefix granularity; if your prompts have unique patient ids embedded it's less effective. We'll estimate with sampling.
[28:18] Marta Reyes: We try to obfuscate patient ids but yes there are unique tokens.

[30:00] Priya Nair: Minimal viable pilot plan (recap): 1) Customer provides 7-day aggregated QPS + 100 golden prompts + env constraints; 2) Redwood synthesizes a replay and proposes two pilot topologies (hosted priority + dedicated warm pool); 3) Run 1 week of replay across 3 model profiles and collect telemetry; 4) Deliver report with cost/latency/quality and recommended configuration.
[30:30] Jordan Ellis: Timeline target: sample by 2027-01-18, run week of 2027-01-25, report by 2027-02-01.

[32:00] Sara Kim: Who is the exec sponsor on Redwood side?
[32:04] Jordan Ellis: I'll be the commercial owner, Priya will be technical lead, Diego for infra, and Diego will loop in the platform reliability folks if needed.

[34:00] Marta Reyes: Quick quality question - do you support reranking/structured output as part of the pipeline? We rely on structured JSON for downstream ingestion.
[34:08] Priya Nair: Yes we support structured outputs and function calling patterns; we'll test those in the golden set.

[36:00] Dev Patel: For the in-cloud mini-run do you need service account creds or can we provide via a bastion?
[36:08] Priya Nair: We can work either way; for hosted pilot credentials are less invasive, for private/dedicated we'll coordinate egress/VPC peering.

[38:00] Jordan Ellis: Any other questions?
[38:05] Marta Reyes: Not right now. We'll aim to get the sample over early next week.

[40:00] Jordan Ellis: Great thanks everyone. Quick recap of next steps — Jordan to send benchmark spreadsheet and pricing, Priya to send pilot topology and suggested warm pool configs, Marta/Liam to provide sample and diagrams. We'll reconvene after we receive the data to schedule the run.
[40:25] Sara Kim: Thanks all.
[40:28] Dev Patel: Thanks.
[40:30] Jordan Ellis: End.

Action items (verbatim list in transcript):
- Jordan: send benchmark template + security pack + SOC2 link
- Priya: propose autoscale/warm pool config and batching windows
- Marta: scrub and upload 7-day sample + golden prompts
- Liam: provide network diagram + retention requirements

Notes about transcription: occasional words garbled (k-v cash instead of kv cache), speaker labels sometimes overlapped, timestamps approximate.

Attachments / references mentioned:

End of transcript.
